title: Lomo Saltado
subtitle: peruvian beef stir-fry with fries
excerpt: A wok-cooked Peruvian stir-fry that combines soy sauce, red wine vinegar and cumin in a single hot pan with beef, peppers and chips. One of the most loved dishes in Peruvian cooking.
sourceNotes: Lomo Saltado reflects the Chinese-Peruvian (Chifa) culinary tradition, where Chinese immigrants adapted wok cooking to Andean ingredients. The result is uniquely Peruvian.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare all the vegetables and measure the sauce ingredients before cooking. This dish moves fast once it starts.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Peruvian stir-fry blending Chinese wok technique with Andean ingredients.

content.text: is Peruvian Chifa cooking at its best. A very hot wok, soy sauce and vinegar combine with beef and peppers in under 10 minutes. The pan-fried potato is mixed through at the end so it absorbs the sauce but stays crisp on the outside.
Get the wok smoking hot before any ingredient goes in. Speed and high heat are the whole point of this dish.

items.prepNote: cut against the grain into 1 cm strips
cut into thick chips, par-fried or oven-baked until golden

content.text: Cook the potato chips until golden in a hot oven at 220C or in a pan of oil. Set aside. Have all other ingredients prepared and close to the wok before you start cooking.

Heat the wok over the highest flame possible for 3 minutes. Add 3 tablespoons of oil. When the oil shimmers and starts to smoke, add the beef in a single layer. Do not stir for 90 seconds. Turn and cook for another 60 seconds. Remove from the wok.
Add the remaining oil. Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the yellow pepper and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the wok. Add the soy sauce and red wine vinegar. The sauce will spit and steam. Toss everything over high heat for 1 minute. Add the tomato wedges and toss for 30 seconds.
Add the cooked potato chips and toss gently so they absorb some sauce without breaking. Scatter with coriander and serve immediately with rice.

attrs.issue: Beef is steaming rather than searing

content.text: The wok is not hot enough, or too much beef went in at once. Cook in two batches and make sure the wok is smoking before each one goes in.

attrs.issue: Sauce is too sharp or salty

content.text: Reduce the soy sauce by 1 tablespoon and the vinegar by 1 teaspoon. The balance should be salty, sour and slightly savoury. Adjust to taste before serving.

attrs.issue: Chips go soggy when added to the wok

content.text: Add them at the very last moment and toss just once or twice. The chips should be very crisp before they go in.

Lomo Saltado was born in Lima's Chinatown in the late 19th century. Chinese immigrants adapted wok technique to the ingredients they found in Peru. The result blended two food cultures in a way neither had done before. It is now one of the top five most ordered dishes in Peru. Every home cook and every restaurant has their version.
